Where ambition is nurtured, and every child can flourish
A Kinder, More Human Approach to Education
Oxford Millwood School (previously Oxford Montessori School) is built on a simple belief: where ambition is nurtured, every child can flourish. Set within a beautiful rural environment, we combine small class sizes, outdoor learning and a rigorous academic curriculum to give pupils the space, support and challenge they need to grow academically and personally.
Many of our pupils arrive bright, curious and full of potential, but have lost confidence in environments that didn’t fully understand their needs. Through highly personalised pathways, therapeutic support and strong, values-driven relationships, we help young people reconnect with learning and rediscover what they are capable of.
Here, pupils find their voice again.
Inspection Excellence
We’re proud to share that OMS has achieved an outstanding inspection outcome. We met and often exceeded every standard, were found fully compliant, and received a Significant Strength for pupil nurture. This rare commendation, the first ever issued by the lead inspector, marks an exceptional achievement for our whole community.
Our Educational Approach
We add real value to every child’s learning by engaging diverse learners with different needs and styles. Our staff bring deep knowledge of child development, exceptional communication, and a passion for inspiring young minds. This combination sparks curiosity, builds confidence, and helps every pupil discover what makes them truly exceptional.
Our Philosophy
We’re reshaping education by refusing to limit children to narrow definitions of achievement. We believe potential is universal, creativity equals academic ability, and every child has something valuable to offer. Education should open doors. By discovering strengths early, we fuel ambition, shape identity and build the confidence children need to thrive.
Our Sites
OMS Primary School
OMS Seniors
OMS Senior School was a truly transformative experience for my son. He went from hating school to wanting to go every day
Camilla Buckley, Parent
Many pupils at the school have arrived with a background of disrupted learning and little self-belief. The school takes great care to ensure that pupils regain their self-confidence and motivation to work and consequently start achieving their potential.
Independent Schools Association Inspector – 2024
The location is idyllic, but it is the staff that really make the difference… they think outside the box, recognise each child for their individual talents, and come up with creative and effective solutions.
The school’s highly nurturing environment supports pupils exceptionally well, both within the classroom and outside.
Independent Schools Association Inspector – 2024
In my view, all schools should be like OMS. Their ethos and aims are universal and right for young people in the 21st century.
Independent Schools Association Inspector – 2019
After a couple of days at Forest Farm School, I began to act more like myself and the person I wanted to be.
The school works tirelessly to fulfil each child’s potential, offering the right qualifications at the right level.
Camilla Buckley, Parent

OMS Seniors
Book a Visit
Apply for a Place
At OMS Seniors, we believe in respect, kindness and compassion; perseverance and commitment; creativity and individuality; gratitude and hope.
Our mission is to give each student the space and support to grow into a thoughtful, confident and capable adult. We combine academic rigour with a deeply human – and humane – approach to education.
What Makes OMS Seniors Different
A Broad, Integrated Curriculum
OMS Seniors delivers a curriculum that combines academic depth with creativity, independence, and purposeful real-world learning. It ensures students are fully prepared for GCSE success while developing into confident, capable, and resilient young adults with the skills and knowledge to thrive in their future education and beyond.
Students follow a diverse and balanced programme, including:
Outdoor Learning & Eco Ethos
Outdoor learning is a defining feature of OMS Seniors. Our 10-acre rural site provides daily opportunities for hands-on discovery, environmental study and physical wellbeing.
Students benefit from:
This approach nurtures grounded, environmentally conscious young people who understand their impact on the world.
Enrichment Opportunities
Enrichment is not an extra – it’s embedded throughout the school experience. These opportunities deepen learning, develop character and broaden personal interests.
At OMS Seniors, we treat students as young adults, giving them real responsibility, a genuine voice, and the respect they deserve. Positive relationships between staff and students are built on mutual trust, respect, and support, creating a learning environment where every individual feels valued and empowered to succeed.
We place strong emphasis on developing essential 21st-century skills, including critical thinking, problem-solving, teamwork, and time management, alongside character, creativity, and self-awareness. By the time our students leave, we aim for them to be not just exam-ready, but world-ready – caring, thoughtful, independent, and equipped with the confidence and adaptability to continue learning throughout life.

Oxford Millwood School provides a nurturing and inclusive environment where students with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) are supported to thrive.
Our experienced SEND team works closely with students, families and teaching staff to identify individual needs, remove barriers to learning and put effective support strategies in place. We focus on helping every child feel safe, valued and confident in their learning.
Support is personalised and responsive, encouraging students to develop independence, resilience and a positive attitude towards learning. We work in strong partnership with parents and carers to ensure each child receives the right support at the right time.
Outdoor Learning is a valued part of life at OMS Seniors. Set within a rural environment, students regularly engage in outdoor activities that support wellbeing, confidence and practical learning. Structured outdoor sessions and curriculum-linked experiences encourage resilience, teamwork and problem-solving, while providing opportunities for reflection and personal growth beyond the classroom setting.
Life Beyond the Classroom
Learning at OMS Seniors extends far beyond lessons. Students take part in enrichment activities, educational visits, community involvement and real-world learning opportunities that support independence and life skills. These experiences help young people build confidence, develop social awareness and prepare for future pathways, including further education, employment and adult life.

pageCache.text:
School Inspection Reports
Our inspection reports offer an independent insight into life at Oxford Millwood School.
Reports published under our previous name, Oxford Montessori School, remain fully relevant today. They reflect the high standards we uphold, our commitment to nurturing every child, and the strong culture of care and wellbeing that defines our school.
We invite you to explore the reports below to learn more about our approach and our recent inspection outcomes.

Curriculum
At Oxford Millwood School, our curriculum is designed to nurture confident, curious and capable learners from Reception through to Year 11.
Built on a thoughtful blend of proven educational approaches and enriched by modern best practice, we offer a broad, balanced and creative learning journey that supports every child to thrive.
Primary (Reception – Year 6)
Our primary curriculum blends the National Curriculum with a child-centred approach offering rich project-based learning without the pressures of SATs. Children enjoy specialist teaching in Music, Drama, PE, Spanish, Computing and Forest School, supported by flexible grouping and a nurturing focus on the whole child.
Senior School (Years 7 – 11)
Our senior curriculum is values-driven and academically ambitious.
Key Stage 3 offers a broad range of subjects: English, Maths, Science, Humanities, Spanish, PSHE, Computing, Creative Arts and Sport, plus an enrichment carousel.
Key Stage 4 offers GCSEs, Functional Skills, ASDAN, Art Awards, Food & Cookery, Spanish, History and the Duke of Edinburgh Award, alongside personalised support and varied assessments.
Careers Education & Work Experience
From an early age, pupils begin exploring their strengths and future possibilities. Our careers programme provides:
Impartial guidance on GCSE and post-16 pathways
Support to challenge stereotypes and broaden aspirations

pageCache.pageTitle: Create holiday club - Oxford Millwood School
pageCache.text:
Create holiday club
OPEN 08:30am to 4:30pm
Welcome to Create – the holiday club where curiosity blossoms, friendships grow and imaginations run wild.
At Create we believe holidays are a time to explore, learn, unwind and have fantastic fun – not just pass the time. Nestled on a beautiful rural site just 3 miles from Oxford city centre, Create Holiday Club offers something truly special: a safe and inspiring setting where children aged 3 to 11 can explore our amazing outdoor environment, join in a whole range of creative art and craft activities, take part in sport and sensory play and have entertainment experiences that they will remember long after the new school term begins.
Our experienced team bring professionalism and excitement to every day at Create. Children will be encouraged to build confidence, learn new skills and make friends all in a warm, diverse and inclusive environment dedicated to them having as much fun as possible.
What We Offer
We are open 08:30am to 4:30pm and we operate in every school holiday except Christmas. We are also closed on public holidays and school INSET days.
There is no such thing as a ‘standard’ day at Create but it will likely include:
Our staff
All staff are carefully chosen for their enthusiasm, professionalism and dedication. Almost all work in education full time as teachers or teaching assistants, all are DBS checked and first aid trained staff are always on hand. As part of Oxford Millwood school we apply the highest standards of safeguarding and health and safety practice to make sure children have fun whilst staying safe. At Create Holiday Club we encourage independence, respect, holistic development, diversity and inclusion.
Contact
Create Holiday Club Manager: Gemma Foster
Deputy Create Holiday Club Manager: Becky Green
Email: create@oxfordmontessori.co.uk
We are usually with the children during the day so telephone contact is limited. If your matter is urgent please call 01865 352065 or text 07855 101213.
In a world full of screens and structured schedules, Create Holiday Club offers a refreshing alternative: time to breathe, time to build, time to play for real. Here children grow resilient, creative and socially confident – not just entertained.
Book your child’s place today and let them experience a holiday where they can truly create friendships and memories.
Book a place
Create FAQs
Create Terms and Conditions

Exam Results
The results our young people achieve are all the more remarkable because they are gained positively and without pressure or cramming.
Students are not steered towards or away from subjects to improve overall outcomes; instead, they are encouraged to choose subjects that reflect their interests, strengths and ambitions.
The wide range of abilities seen from year to year is a testament to both the individuality of our learners and the dedication behind their achievements.
The OMS Approach
Our pupils achieve strong results driven by self-motivation and genuine engagement with their learning.
Most examinations are taken during the May/June examination session, with some subjects also offered in November where appropriate.
Exam rooms are light, airy and comfortable, helping students feel calm and supported.
Our approach to examinations is as relaxed and informal as possible, while remaining fully compliant with regulations.
OMS is accredited by the Joint Council for Qualifications (JCQ), Cambridge International Examinations (CIE), ASDAN and Trinity.
2026 GCSE Results
Results in English and the individual Sciences were particularly strong, with 100% of students achieving grades 5–9 in these subjects.
High grades were achieved across a broad range of subjects, with 50% or more of students studying Maths, English, Geography and Art achieving grades 7–9.

pageCache.pageTitle: OMS Primary School - Oxford Millwood School
pageCache.text:
OMS Primary School
Book a Visit
Apply for a Place
OMS Primary is located on a peaceful, rural 10-acre campus. There are two mixed-age classes for children aged 4 to 16, staffed by qualified teachers and assistants.
The school ethos centres on respect, independence, and personal growth: children are encouraged to take responsibility for their own learning, and our learning environment is shaped around their interests and developmental needs.
A Balanced Approach
OMS Primary combines the structure of the National Curriculum with an emphasis on independence and child-led learning. Children learn through a mix of individual exploration, hands-on activities and rich, cross-curricular projects that connect subjects such as geography, history, science, maths, literacy and the arts.
Alongside this creative approach, we place a strong emphasis on literacy and assessment through our Read, Write & Grow approach:
This balanced model gives children the freedom to explore, the space to build confidence and the structure to thrive academically.
Outdoor Learning & Forest School
We strongly believe in the power of nature: Primary children spend at least 20% of their school week outdoors.
Our outdoor spaces include woodland (coppice), meadow, greenhouse, footpaths, and willow domes.
Weekly Forest School sessions encourage children to build dens, observe wildlife, learn survival skills, care for nature, and work with tools — all in a safe, structured setting.
These experiences foster resilience, independence, creativity, and a deep connection with the natural world.
Inclusion, Support & Student Voice
The school has a Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENDCo) to support learners who need additional help.
We welcome children with diverse linguistic backgrounds; English as an Additional Language (EAL) support is available.
Pupils are encouraged to take responsibility for their learning, using available resources, and contributing ideas to shape their education.
Parents are key partners: there are regular parent–teacher meetings, open classrooms, and community events like sports day, performances, and garden cafés.
Eco-Philosophy & Sustainability
OMS Primary participates in the Eco-Schools programme; children are actively involved via an Eco Council.
Environmental practices include reducing plastic use and caring for the woodland: the school maintains over 2,000 trees in its coppice wood.
Through these practices, students develop environmental awareness, responsibility, and a commitment to sustainability.

Admissions
At Oxford Millwood School, we believe that every child is unique and deserves an education that recognises, respects and nurtures their individual potential.
We offer a calm, purposeful and inclusive learning environment where children are encouraged to develop independence, confidence and a lifelong love of learning – at a pace that is right for them.
Whether your child is joining us in the early years, transitioning into our primary or senior provision, or moving at a key stage in their education, our admissions process is designed to be warm, transparent and personal.
Open Day
Thursday 15th October, 10am – 2pm.
We have a new name, but our school offers the same genuine care, academic ambition and belief in every child. See how our small classes, personalised pathways and strong SEND expertise give pupils the support, challenge and confidence they need to succeed — especially those who may not have thrived in larger settings.
Your Child’s Admissions Journey
We understand that choosing a school is one of the most important decisions you will make for your child. Our admissions journey is designed to be thoughtful, supportive and centred around getting to know your child as an individual.
Our bespoke and straightforward admissions process reflects the values of our school and typically follows these steps:
1. Make an Initial Enquiry
Reach out to our friendly Admissions Team to ask questions, request a prospectus, or simply start a conversation. We’re here to listen and help.
2. Book a Personal Tour or Attend an Open Day
Please do take the time to come and see us in action. The best way is to come and experience the school for yourself – ideally with your child.
Book your visit now.
3. Register Your Interest
If you feel that our school could be the right fit, we’ll invite you to register your interest and begin the next steps.
4. Offer Stage
The final step – There is no entrance examination to join our school – we are proudly all-ability. There’s a straightforward administration process and an opportunity for both the school and the family to reflect briefly to ensure that we are the right fit for each other. At that point an offer would be made.
5. Secure Your Place
Once we receive your completed admissions forms and deposit, your child’s place at our school is confirmed.
6. Your Child’s Journey Begins
From here, the adventure truly starts. We’ll work closely with you to ensure a smooth, supported transition into school life.

Safeguarding
At Oxford Millwood School, safeguarding is our top priority.
We are committed to ensuring every child feels safe, valued and listened to. All staff understand their responsibilities and act immediately on any concerns. We follow Keeping Children Safe in Education 2025, Working Together to Safeguard Children, and Oxfordshire’s local safeguarding procedures.
Our Designated Safeguarding Leads oversee all safeguarding matters, ensuring concerns are recorded accurately and shared with the appropriate agencies when needed. We take a zero-tolerance approach to bullying, harassment, abuse and discrimination, and children are taught how to stay safe both in school and online.
Safeguarding applies across all our sites and activities, and we work closely with families and external professionals so every child can thrive in a safe and supportive environment.

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to Oxford Millwood School – a place where curiosity thrives, individuality is celebrated, and learning is an adventure.
At OMS, we believe that every child is unique, capable and full of potential. Our mission is to nurture confident, compassionate and creative learners who are inspired to discover the world around them with joy and purpose. Grounded in curiosity-led, inquiry-based learning and supported by a culture of respect and care, our community is built on trusting relationships between pupils, families and staff.
From our youngest learners in early years through to our seniors, we offer an environment that champions curiosity, independence and resilience. We are committed to unlocking each child’s talents by providing meaningful experiences that connect academic growth with real-world understanding. Throughout our school, children enjoy open spaces, creative classrooms, and opportunities to explore, collaborate and grow at their own pace.
Partnership with families is at the heart of what we do. We work closely with you to understand and support your child’s journey, nurturing their strengths and guiding them through challenges with compassion and confidence. Together, we build a learning experience that is personalised, purposeful and joyful.
Thank you for taking the time to explore our school. We look forward to welcoming you into our vibrant community – where every child can flourish and where learning truly begins with wonder.
Katie Townsend, Headteacher
